text:
The Islanders are 7-6-2, close to .500, and closer to it than their chances deserve. They get 46.7% of the expected goals and allow 3.39 per hour, a leaky number. Their goaltending has saved about eight and a half goals more than expected, which is why they're even with opponents on the scoreboard (42 for, 43 against).

Semyon Varlamov has been better than his record over his last five starts: 5.0 goals saved above expected and a 1-2-1 record to show for it. NHL.com's Stefen Rosner reported Ilya Sorokin was set to start against New Jersey tonight.

The bright spots are up front. Brayden Schenn's line with Emil Heineman and Victor Eklund has outscored teams 6-0 at five on five on 63% of the chances. The Bo Horvat line with Kyle Palmieri and Simon Holmstrom creates a lot (4.7 expected goals per hour) and gives a lot back (3.36), and it's been outscored 6-4. Matthew Schaefer and Logan Stanley are a 56% pair, while Adam Pelech and Ryan Pulock sit at 42%.

The help may be close: Rosner reported Mathew Barzal and Matias Maccelli were out of non-contact jerseys this week. Our numbers give the Islanders a 24% playoff chance on an 86-point pace. The goaltending can keep them close; the chances have to come back for anything more.
headline: The Islanders are getting outchanced and getting away with it
